root_cause.text: The AMD DCN stream encoder creation code in `dcn351_resource.c` (and related DCN resource files) used `eng_id` directly as an index into the 5-element `stream_enc_regs[]` array without validating that it was within bounds, allowing `eng_id == 5` or negative values to cause an out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states “eng_id is used directly as an index into stream_enc_regs[], which has only 5 entries” and that “When eng_id is 5 (ENGINE_ID_DIGF) or negative, this can access memory past the end of the array”; the patch fixes this by replacing `if (eng_id <= ENGINE_ID_DIGF)` with `if (eng_id < 0 || eng_id >= ARRAY_SIZE(stream_enc_regs)) return NULL;` before using `&stream_enc_regs[eng_id]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject invalid stream encoder IDs before mapping register blocks to prevent out-of-bounds access during encoder creation.
intent_record.what: The condition that previously accepted only `eng_id <= ENGINE_ID_DIGF` and assigned `vpg_inst`/`afmt_inst` inside that branch was replaced with a range check `eng_id < 0 || eng_id >= ARRAY_SIZE(stream_enc_regs)` that returns `NULL`; the assignments to `vpg_inst` and `afmt_inst` were moved after the check and are now unconditional for valid IDs.
intent_record.how: At runtime, invalid stream encoder IDs are now rejected explicitly, preventing out-of-bounds access when selecting register blocks and ensuring only valid `eng_id` values are used to create the VPG and AFMT instances.
